text:
Devin: heads up — we observed canary exposure dropping to 0% in eu-west when quota throttles hit, even though the rollout is 10% for Standard tier. looks like the router is falling back to the baseline variant before the rollout policy is evaluated.
Maya: odd, it should respect rollout scope per-tier before fallback. can you paste the router logs?
Devin: paste: `router: route_id=embed-prod, tier=standard, region=eu-west, desired_weights={v1:90,v2-canary:10}, quota_left=0, action=fallback->v1`
Sam: ah this is the classic precedence bug — quota check happens earlier than rollout selection. when quota==0 we force fallback to cheapest compatible variant which ignores scoped rollout.
Ana: that's going to break A/B experiments for customers — their canaries never get exposure if quota bursts on baseline are exhausted. we need a fix that either: (1) honors rollout allocation and deducts from a per-variant quota bucket, or (2) surfaces shadow-fallback metrics so PMs know exposures were suppressed.
Rohit: +1 for per-variant buckets. implementation idea: when routing picks weights it should do an availability check that returns "available but will incur quota" vs "unavailable". only if unavailable should we pick a fallback. so v2-canary would be "available but quota-limited" and the router can still route a small % and let quota meter in parallel.
Maya: agreed. current behavior is too binary. Also telemetry problem: console currently aggregates by model family (embed-prod) so you can't tell if v2 latency regressed because traffic never hit it. we should emit `variant` tag on the request span and create a per-variant time-series in the console.
Sam: schema update needed: metrics tag list -> add variant,tier,region,route_id. Prom endpoint will remain the same but queryable by these labels. beware cardinality blowup for free-form variant ids. we should whitelist variants per route.
Ana: UX ask: in Rollouts UI show two numbers: "requested exposure" and "actual exposure" (actual = post-fallback traffic). also add a small explanation tooltip: "actual exposure may be lower if quota, regional capacity, or hard-fallback policies trigger."
Devin: quick patch proposal I sketched in config form: ```{ "routing_policy": "weighted", "weights": {"v1": 90, "v2-canary": 10}, "quota_behavior": "respect_rollout_with_variant_buckets" }``` basically create ephemeral buckets for rollout variants that deplete from the customer's quota when used.
Rohit: note we need grace for burst windows — if a customer has a monthly commit and temporary per-minute cap is 0, we still want canary to get its tiny share. maybe add `rollout_reserve_percent` that guarantees X% of their capacity for rollout traffic until the bucket is empty.
Maya: ops concern: if we reserve for many customers that could starve baseline production. propose: reserve only when tier==standard+ and rollout_exposure <= 5% and region has >20% spare capacity. otherwise fallback like today.
Sam: implementation steps: 1) router: reorder evaluation so rollout selection happens before hard fallback; 2) add variant-availability check (available|quota-limited|unavailable); 3) update quota service to support ephemeral variant buckets + reserve logic; 4) emit variant tag in tracing/metrics; 5) console: add actual vs requested exposure panel + per-variant series.
Ana: can we ship a minimal telemetry-only change first? at least show suppressed exposure so PMs know canary wasn't exercised. that's lower risk.
Devin: I can prototype telemetry change today. will add trace/span tag `variant` and a counter `routing.exposure.actual{variant,tier,region,route}`.
infra-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-change -> staging (job 8421). status: queued. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Rohit: timeline idea: telemetry-only to staging this week, prod next week. router + quotas refactor targeted for the sprint after.
Maya: looks good. @Devin drop a short RFC in eng-platform so we can sync on edge cases (multi-region fallbacks, cross-tier promotions). also include expected metric names and a small dashboard mock.
Devin: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
